'''Edward Allan Frieman''' (January 19, 1926 – April 11, 2013) was an American physicist who worked on [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and [[nuclear fusion]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11510002.html|title=Frieman, E. A.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> He was the director of the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]] from 1986 through 1996, and then the senior vice president of science and technology at the [[Science Applications International Corporation]] from 1996 on until his death in 2013.<ref>[http://www.lajollalight.com/2013/04/12/former-scripps-director-prominent-physicist-and-government-advisor-edward-a-frieman-has-died-at-87/ Former Scripps Director, prominent physicist, and government advisor Edward A. Frieman has died at 87, La Jolla Light] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130507010118/http://www.lajollalight.com/2013/04/12/former-scripps-director-prominent-physicist-and-government-advisor-edward-a-frieman-has-died-at-87/ |date=2013-05-07 }}. Accessed 13 April 2013</ref><ref>[http://scilib.ucsd.edu/sio/biogr/Frieman_Biogr.pdf Biography of Edward Allan Frieman by Dennis Monday] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429142322/http://scilib.ucsd.edu/sio/biogr/Frieman_Biogr.pdf |date=April 29, 2013 }}. Accessed 13 April 2013</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Frieman was born in New York in 1926. During [[World War II]], he served as a deep-sea diving officer and was a participant in the atomic tests at [[Bikini Atoll]]. After the war, [[Columbia University]] granted him a bachelor's degree in engineering in 1946. He then received his master's and doctorate degrees in physics from the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]] in 1948 and 1951 respectively.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130430164144/http://articles.latimes.com/2013/apr/28/local/la-me-edward-frieman-20130429 Researcher was a leading figure in American science in] [[Los Angeles Times]], Accessed 2013-05-01.</ref>

Frieman spent 25 years at [[Princeton University]], becoming a professor of astrophysical science in 1961. It was during this period of time where he was noted to have advised [[Charles Kennel]] on his doctoral thesis.<ref name=":0" />

In 1979, he was nominated by President [[Jimmy Carter]] to be the director of [[Office of Science]] within the [[United States Department of Energy]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Energy Nomination of Edward Allan Frieman To Be Director of the Office of Energy Research. {{!}} The American Presidency Project|url=https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/department-energy-nomination-edward-allan-frieman-be-director-the-office-energy-research|access-date=2020-08-08|website=www.presidency.ucsb.edu}}</ref> He served in the position from 1980 to 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Former Directors|url=https://www.energy.gov/science/former-directors|access-date=2020-08-08|website=Energy.gov|language=en}}</ref>

In 1981, he became an executive vice president of the [[Science Applications International Corporation]], a high-tech company in La Jolla. In 1986, Frieman became the director of the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]], a research institution at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. Frieman also served on the boards of the [[American University in Paris]] and the [[U.S.-Israel Binational Science Foundation]].

== Awards and honors ==
In 1962, Frieman was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1962&unit_id=APS&institution=Princeton+University|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> and then inducted into the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/edward-a-frieman-fou8ra/|title=Edward Frieman|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Edward+A.+Frieman&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> In 2002, Frieman was awarded the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] by APS.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2007-01-12|title=APS Announces Award Recipients|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1537924|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=55|issue=12|pages=74–75|doi=10.1063/1.1537924|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Frieman is the father of theoretical astrophysicist [[Joshua A. Frieman]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIP Oral History |url=https://repository.aip.org/frieman-joshua-2020-october-6 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=repository.aip.org/oral-history-interviews-ohi}}</ref>
